Each question shows its Insight page and number. Where Insight lets several questions share information, that information is repeated in each box.

Question 11 mark

The table below gives the exam results and number of hours spent studying for a different group of students.

A non-linear scatterplot for this data is also shown.

No. of hours studied4561222.53.64
Exam result183038252224282220
No. of hours studied789.83.45.67.86.23.11.5
Exam result526598233267422228
No. of hours studied6.37.23.56.78.46.78.46.75.5
Exam result425123526752675134

A squared transformation will be applied to the variable No. of hours studied and can be used to linearise the scatterplot.

The equation of the least squares regression line for this squared transformation is closest to

A.(exam result)2 = 15.4 + 0.76 × no. hours studied ✓
B.exam result = 0.76 + 15.4 × (no. of hours studied)2 ✓
C.exam result = 15.4 + 0.76 × no. of hours studied ✓
D.(No. of hours studied)2 = 15.4 + 0.76 × exam result ✓
E.exam result = 15.4 + 0.76 × (no. hours studied)2 ✓
CAS with x = (hours studied)², y = exam result: a = 15.4, b = 0.76. Only the explanatory variable is squared.

Question 21 mark

Jaxon uses the following data to generate the scatterplot below.

x12345678910
y250241232212189148101492214

The scatterplot shows that the data is non-linear.

Jaxon performs the squared transformation to the variable y.

He then fits a least squares line to the transformed data, with x as the explanatory variable.

Using this line, the predicted value for y when x is equal to 5 is closest to

A.16 852 ✓
B.361 ✓
C.230 ✓
D.182 ✓
E.118 ✓
y² = 73 661.5 − 8115.6x; y² = 73 661.5 − 8115.6 × 5, so y = √33 083.5 = 181.89 ≈ 182

Question 31 mark

The heights of seedlings are measured weekly to track their progress. The data is shown below.

Age (weeks)012345678
Average height (cm)6.16.47.59.612.018.229.446.161.2

A squared transformation of age is performed. The equation of the least squares regression line for the transformed data is

Average height = 2.43 + 0.856 × (age)2

At approximately what age were the plants when the average height was 20 cm?

A.4.4 weeks ✓
B.4.5 weeks ✓
C.19.6 weeks ✓
D.20.5 weeks ✓
E.345 weeks ✓
20 = 2.43 + 0.856 × age² → age² = 20.53 → age = 4.5 weeks

The equation of the least squares line for the transformed data is

C.temperature = 182.26 + 203.38 × log(time) ✓

Question 71 mark

The data below shows the temperature and the number of visitors to a local pool each day over a 10-day period.

Temperature (°C)1723273133
Number of visitors63211294312233
Temperature (°C)3238241817
Number of visitors2602512057753

A reciprocal transformation is applied to the temperature in order to attempt to linearise the data.

The equation of the least squares line for the transformed data is

number of visitors = 494.7 − 7191 × 1temperature

Which one of the following changes has occurred after the transformation?

A.The correlation coefficient has become weaker from 0.830 to −0.917 ✓
B.The correlation coefficient has become stronger from 0.830 to −0.917 ✓
C.The coefficient of determination has increased from 0.670 to 0.955 ✓
D.The coefficient of determination has decreased from 0.841 to 0.690 ✓
E.The coefficient of determination has decreased from 0.841 to 0.670 ✓
Before: r = 0.830; after (x = 1/temperature): r = −0.917. |r| is larger, so the association is stronger (r² rises from 0.690 to 0.841).
Insight GM1 U3 Data Analysis p.21 Q31 · shares information with Insight Q30–32

x0123
y142580
1y10.250.040.0125
x4567
y2001000400025 000
1y0.0050.0010.000250.00004

1y = 0.512 − 0.10x

Insight GM2 U3 Data Analysis p.27 Q12
aIn the table above, complete the missing values for the transformed values of y.1 mark
1/25 = 0.04, 1/200 = 0.005
bThe equation is used to predict that, for a particular value of x, y = 1.587.

4D

Choosing and applying the right transformation

Done
Date
Multiple choiceCircle one answer. 2 marks
Question 111 mark

Jaxon uses the following data to generate the scatterplot below.

x12345678910
y250241232212189148101492214

The scatterplot shows that the data is non-linear.

To linearise the data, Jaxon could apply which of the following sets of transformations?

A.x2 or 1y ✓
B.x2 or y2 ✓
C.x2 or log y ✓
D.y2 or log x ✓
E.y2 or 1x ✓
Decreasing and curving down (concave down): the circle of transformations gives x² or y². These are the only ones that could linearise the data.
Insight GM1 U3 Data Analysis p.17 Q15 · shares information with Insight Q15–16
Question 121 mark

Data on the cooling of an object in a laboratory freezer was recorded.

These times are shown in the table below.

Time (min)12345678910
Temperature (°C)21011461453212851.30.2

Which one of the following transformations would be appropriate in order to linearise this data?

A.1time, 1temp, log(time), log(temp) ✓
B.1temp, log(temp), time2 ✓
C.log(time), time2, temp2 ✓
D.1time, log(time), temp2 ✓
E.1time, 1temp, log(temp), time2 ✓
Decreasing and curving up (concave up): the circle of transformations gives log x, 1/x, log y or 1/y.
